transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-06
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood), Maya Chen (Acme ML), Diego Rivera (Acme SRE), Lina Gomez (Acme Product), Tom Wu (Acme Security)

Auto Summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles, demo of benchmark dashboard, initial quality/latency numbers for INT8 and FP8 on a 3B/7B model family. Action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, I'll hand off to Priya in a minute to go through the quant profiles, quick intro: acme team, thanks for carving out the time.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Hey thanks Jordan, Maya here. we want to see how INT8 vs FP8 would affect our throughput and if quality drop is acceptable for our agent responses.
[00:22] Jordan Lee: totally, goal here is practical: show you Optimize's recommendations, run-through of the dashboard, and then outline a pilot. Priya?
[00:30] Priya Nair: hi all, Priya (SE). i'll share my screen, ok - can everyone see the dashboard? (crosstalk) looks good. so first quick primer: INT8 is the higher quant, lower precision but big perf wins on most GPUs; FP8 keeps more dynamic range so often preserves quality but requires newer runtimes/hardware.
[01:05] Priya Nair: here's a sample run we did with a 7B-ish open model on our runtime - baseline FP16 serving at median 120ms per token, batch size 1, INT8 median moved to ~85ms, FP8 sits around 95ms in our tests. quality delta we measured with BLEU-style and semantic-sim metrics - INT8 had 2-4% relative drop on average, FP8 0.5-1.5% depending on prompt complexity.
[01:50] Diego Rivera: those numbers look promising, but what's noise - like for chat sessions with long KV caches, does INT8 break the cache or cause accumulative drift?
[02:05] Priya Nair: good question - our runtime keeps the KV cache in FP16 by default to avoid drift; quantization is applied to model weights and some activations during inference. for very long context sequences we saw small divergence in edge cases, we annotate those in the benchmark with worst-case examples.
[02:35] Maya Chen: when you say "we saw" who runs these, is it Redwood or do we run on our infra?
[02:43] Jordan Lee: for the pilot we can do both: we can run initial benchmarking on Redwood hosted to get fast numbers, then replicate on your Dedicated nodes or on-prem with your quant profiles. we'll provide scripts.
[02:55] Lina Gomez: What's the recommended approach to pick FP8 vs INT8? is it just a threshold on allowable quality loss?
[03:05] Priya Nair: usually it's driven by SLOs and unit economics - if you have strict quality targets (e.g., >98% on your eval) FP8 is safer, but if cost/latency are dominant and you can tolerate a small drop, INT8 often wins. Also model family matters - some architectures quantize better. Optimize will auto-suggest profiles per model+workload.
[03:35] Samir Patel: adding to that, we use kernel selection and quant-aware compilation so some INT8 paths on certain GPUs are actually faster than FP8 depending on tensor core support.
[03:50] Tom Wu: security question - does quantization change anything for data residency or encryption? we need to keep all logs and KV cache in our VPC and keys in our KMS.
[04:05] Priya Nair: quantization is purely weights/runtime, it doesn't change data flows. for Dedicated and Private deployments everything stays in your VPC; KMS integration is supported. we do persist audit logs and tracebacks to customer S3 or blob with encryption at rest; can share SOC2 docs.
[04:35] Diego Rivera: how about GPU compatibility - FP8 needs newer drivers right? will you manage that on Dedicated?
[04:43] Jordan Lee: yes FP8 currently requires more modern runtimes and often NVIDIA driver stacks that support TF32/FP8 kernels; on Dedicated we manage the stack if you want us to, or we provide the exact AMI/container spec for your infra team.
[04:58] Maya Chen: performance numbers - you quoted median token latencies, what about p95/p99 and throughput for batching?
[05:10] Priya Nair: on the same benchmark, p95 for FP16 baseline was around 210ms, INT8 p95 dropped to 150ms, FP8 around 165ms. For batching throughput INT8 showed ~1.6x higher tokens/sec vs FP16 at batch sizes 4-16. we included tail-latency breakdowns in the shared spreadsheet.
[05:45] Lina Gomez: are there cases where INT8 shows large regressions in quality?
[05:52] Priya Nair: more likely on models with very narrow dynamic ranges or custom attention patterns; also hallucination-sensitive prompts sometimes degrade. we advise running your prompt set against both profiles; Optimize's delta scoring highlights prompts with biggest diffs.
[06:18] Maya Chen: can you demo the delta scoring?
[06:22] Priya Nair: sure, switching to the evaluation tab - here's a matrix: prompt groups on rows, profile columns - color-coded diffs. you can click into a prompt to see side-by-side outputs (left FP16, right INT8). notice this example where INT8 drops a key numeric detail by one digit - flagged as high severity.
[07:00] Diego Rivera: nice — how are these diffs computed? purely BLEU/ROUGE or semantic embedding distance?
[07:07] Priya Nair: we use an ensemble: lexical (BLEU-like), embedding cosine, and a task-specific classifier if you provide one. for Acme we recommended a custom scorer focusing on entity accuracy and instruction-following.
[07:30] Maya Chen: client-side constraints - we likely need to keep models in our subnet and HSM-managed keys. is Redwood able to support HSM or BYOK?
[07:40] Jordan Lee: yes, BYOK and HSM integration are supported for Private/Dedicated. we do require a short proof-of-authority exchange for key rotation and we can align with your security team on policies.
[07:55] Tom Wu: ok we'll follow up with specifics.
[08:00] Priya Nair: back to latency: one more nuance is KV cache handling - if you have heavy reuse we can enable prefix caching which can dramatically reduce per-token compute; Optimize will detect high prefix similarity and recommend caching. in some cases caching + INT8 yields huge win with almost no quality loss.
[08:30] Diego Rivera: what's the best way to measure the economic impact? token cost vs instance cost?
[08:36] Samir Patel: we output unit economics: tokens/sec per dollar, and end-to-end latencies at different loads. the spreadsheet has a cost model with committed vs on-demand pricing for Dedicated and hosted.
[08:55] Maya Chen: can we see an example pilot plan?
[09:00] Jordan Lee: yes - typical pilot: week 1 - baseline runs on hosted with your prompt set; week 2 - tuned quant profiles + FP8/INT8 comparisons; week 3 - replicate on Dedicated / your infra and finalize recommendations. deliverables: benchmark sheet, quality diffs, suggested profile YAMLs, and runbook for deployment.
[09:30] Lina Gomez: are there any out-of-the-box profiles for Llama-ish models? we don't want to hand-tune everything.
[09:38] Priya Nair: we publish curated profiles for common model families and Optimize will auto-adapt. for custom forks we do a quick calibration pass.
[09:50] Maya Chen: ok regarding model versions - if we pin a version for a rollout how do we handle fallback if a quant profile causes regressions in production?
[09:59] Samir Patel: rollout policies support canary and automatic rollback; you can route a percent of traffic and monitor quality metrics. Redwood can auto-fallback to a higher-precision variant if thresholds are crossed.
[10:15] Diego Rivera: about metrics — can you push traces to our observability stack? we use Datadog.
[10:22] Jordan Lee: yes we have tracing hooks and can stream metrics/logs to Datadog, Splunk, or send to your S3.
[10:30] Tom Wu: one more compliance thing - do you keep traces of the textual request bodies in logs? we need redact rules for PII.
[10:38] Priya Nair: we support configurable log redaction and token-level masking; you can opt out of storing full request bodies and only persist input hashes for auditing.
[10:50] Maya Chen: great. any limitations around languages other than English? our agents use Spanish and Portuguese too.
[10:58] Priya Nair: tradeoffs are similar; quantization effects can be slightly different for multilingual models but our delta scoring will show that. we recommend including representative multilingual prompts in the eval.
[11:12] Jordan Lee: quick point on costs — Dedicated reserved capacity gives best unit economics if you have steady load; hosted is easier to start for benchmarking.
[11:24] Maya Chen: curious about SLOs for tail latency in Dedicated with INT8, can you guarantee p99 for sub-second?
[11:34] Jordan Lee: we offer SLA-backed latency targets for Dedicated tiers; exact numbers depend on instance types and model size. we'll propose targets in the pilot proposal.
[11:45] Lina Gomez: what's the turnaround time to get a Dedicated environment up?
[11:50] Jordan Lee: usually 2-3 weeks for provisioning and validation if you're doing customer-managed infra; if Redwood manages Dedicated we can be faster depending on capacity.
[12:00] Maya Chen: ok let's talk about the benchmark data we need — how many prompts?
[12:06] Priya Nair: 200-500 representative prompts is a sweet spot for initial pass; include edge cases and multilanguage examples.
[12:15] Maya Chen: we'll compile that.
[12:18] Diego Rivera: are sample scripts in python? we prefer that.
[12:21] Priya Nair: yes we have python + JS examples and a small harness that runs side-by-side comparisons and outputs diffs.
[12:30] Jordan Lee: any outstanding blockers from security?
[12:33] Tom Wu: mainly KMS/HSM specifics and SOC2 artifacts. also need to see how RBAC maps to our existing IAM.
[12:42] Jordan Lee: we'll include RBAC mapping guide and SOC2 package in the security docs we send.
[12:47] Lina Gomez: ok wrapping up, can you summarize next steps?
[12:50] Jordan Lee: sure - Jordan to send pilot proposal + pricing; Priya to share quant benchmark spreadsheet and scripts; Acme to provide prompt set and KMS details; schedule pilot kickoff week of 3/16.
[13:05] Maya Chen: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[13:08] Jordan Lee: thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
